sense_notes: Speaker witnessed it. Mandatory slot; scopes over negation (D30).
Speaker was told it. Source is someone else's statement.
Speaker reasoned it out from evidence, did not witness it.
Known without a source: definition, convention, common knowledge.
Speaker is committed to doing it. The commitment half of English 'will' (D31).
Speaker expects it, without commitment. The prediction half of English 'will'.
Offered for testing or discussion, not claimed. A hypothesis, never a finding (D34).
Speaker relies on it as an assumption; the thing being built on.
Speaker knows it may go wrong and says so.
Speaker insists, against pushback. Carries emphasis (D32).
Before now. Present is unmarked.
After now, strictly temporal; intention and prediction are stance (D31).
Piece of the verb ending, before tense. Evidential scopes over it (D32).
Last piece of the embedded verb's ending; makes a clause a complement or a relative clause (D33).
On the argument acted on. Subject is bare.
On the argument that is a place, source or goal of location.
On the possessor, which precedes the possessed.
Sentence-final. The answer supplies the evidential (D30, D33).
Speaker. Takes case markers, nothing else.
Addressee.
Near or just mentioned; person or thing. No gender, no animacy.
Far or earlier mentioned; person or thing.
Accompaniment or instrument. Separate word after its argument.
Beneficiary or purpose.
Origin, cause or source, when the location case is not enough.
Knowing carve, side 1 of 3: known because it was tried or observed to hold. Not by definition (side 2), not belief (side 3). As an argument: a tested fact.
Knowing carve, side 2 of 3: known because that is what the word, rule or convention says. Not tested, not believed. As an argument: a definition, a convention.
Knowing carve, side 3 of 3: held to be so without test or definition. Covers English believe, assume, take for granted. As an argument: a belief.
Error carve, side 1 of 3: a wrong act by someone. The person erred. Not the fault it may have left in the thing (side 2), not what happened at run time (side 3).
Error carve, side 2 of 3: a wrong state in the thing itself, present whether or not anything has gone wrong yet. English bug, defect. Verbal: to be faulty.
Error carve, side 3 of 3: something went wrong when it ran or was used. The event, not its cause. English crash, fail, error at run time. Verbal: to fail.
Asking carve, side 1 of 3: a request to be told something. Same consonant family as the question particle. Not a request for action (side 2), not a check (side 3).
Asking carve, side 2 of 3: a request that someone do something. English please, could you, request. Never a question about facts.
Asking carve, side 3 of 3: asking whether something taken as so actually holds. English confirm, verify with someone, sanity-check. The answer is a stance or evidential.
Change carve, side 1 of 3: change what is broken so that it works. Presupposes a fault or failure. Not alter (side 2), not build (side 3).
Change carve, side 2 of 3: change what already works into something else that works. English modify, update, refactor, tweak. Nothing was broken.
Change carve, side 3 of 3: bring into existence what was not there. English make, create, write from scratch, implement. As an argument: a thing built.

Lumped root (D35): the act of doing something in order to observe what happens. One root for lab experiment, unit test, and trying a thing to see. The evidential carries the result. As an argument: a test, an experiment, an attempt.

The one interrogative root. Bare: what. Before a root as a determiner: which (D44). With location case: where. With 'for': why. With 'with': how, by what means. With the time root: when. With the person root: who. There are no other question words.
A human. Verbal use: to be a person, to be someone. With the interrogative before it: who.
Make something go: execute a program, start a process, operate a machine. Not moving on foot; that is not in the language yet.
Take in what is written or displayed. As an argument: a reading, a read.
Put down in writing or in code. As an argument: a piece of writing, code written.
Direct attention at; examine, inspect. Does not imply finding anything. As an argument: a look, an inspection.
Locate or discover what was looked for or not. Implies success. As an argument: a finding.
Any entity, abstract or concrete. The default noun; use a narrower root when one exists.
What brings something about. Verbal use: to cause. Paired with result.
What is brought about; an outcome, output, the value a test gives. Verbal use: to result, to come out as.
A point or stretch of time. With the interrogative before it: when. Verbal use: to take time, to last.
Identifier of a thing or person: a name, a label, a variable name. Verbal use: to name, to call.
A document or file on a machine; also a page of text. Verbal use: to file, to save as a file.
Set two or more things side by side to see how they differ or agree. As an argument: a comparison.
Find how much or how big by a procedure with a unit. As an argument: a measurement, a measure.
Let time pass until something happens. As an argument: a wait, a delay.
A component of a larger thing. Verbal use: to be part of.
One root: nominal use is a number or quantity, verbal use is to count. English splits these; the language does not (D25).
A location, physical or in a file or system. With the interrogative before it: where. Verbal use: to be located at, to put.
A computer, device or mechanism that runs. Verbal use: to be mechanical, to run automatically.
Large in size, amount or importance. Stative: 'the file bigs' = the file is big. Small is its own root, not big-NEG.
Little in size, amount or importance. Own root; not-big is weaker than small.
Good for its purpose; working well; approved of. Stative. As an argument: a good, a benefit.
Bad for its purpose; working badly; disapproved of. Own root; not-good is weaker than bad.
Identical or equivalent to the thing compared with ('with'). Different = same-NEG; there is no separate root (D25).
Is the case; holds. False = true-NEG; there is no separate root (D25). As an argument: a truth, a fact that holds.
Finished, complete. Stative. Not-done = still in progress. Broken is not a root: use fault verbally (D35).
Earlier than its argument, in time or in order. After its argument like the other relational words. 'this time before' = before now.
Later than its argument, in time or in order. 'test after' = after the test.
Numeral 1. Numerals stand before the root they count, like determiners (D44, D48).
Numeral 2.
Numeral 3.
Numeral 4.
Numeral 5. Base of 6-9: five-one, five-two, five-three, five-four, written solid.
Numeral 10. A numeral before ten multiplies it, anything after adds: two-ten = 20, ten-five = 15, two-ten-five-one = 26.
5+1, written solid. Composed, but listed so the corpus can count it.
5+2, written solid.
5+3, written solid.
5+4, written solid.
